cards.hint: Think about the count noted after the first census.
cards.quote: Since that first census in 1790, five methods of apportionment have been used.
cards.stem: Since the first census, how many different ways to divide seats have been used?

cards.hint: Look for the waiting time after the first meeting.
cards.quote: The actual Enumeration shall be made within three Years after the first Meeting of the Congress of the United States
cards.stem: What period after the first gathering of Congress is set for the actual count?

cards.hint: Focus on the name of the present approach.
cards.quote: The current method used, the Method of Equal Proportions, was adopted by congress in 1941 following the census of 1940.
cards.stem: Which present way of assigning seats followed the census taken in 1940?

cards.hint: Recall the full size mentioned with the one seat start.
cards.quote: Each of the 50 states is given one seat out of the current total of 435.
cards.stem: What is the present total from which every state first gets one seat?
